name: Desert Observatory
desc: A desert observatory ridge under a wheeling night sky: two domes stand black against the Milky Way, the whole star field turns slowly about the celestial pole so nothing is ever still, airglow banks along the horizon and a dome slit breathes a thread of red; a deep cold star-field, a rich galactic-core night, a brighter moonlit sky, an abstracted cyan star chart, or a monochrome ink nocturne.

energy.doc: overall brightness — star luminance, Milky Way glow and twinkle amplitude

scale.doc: dome size and Milky Way band width — from a distant ridge to close monumental domes and a broad galaxy

density.doc: how many stars fill the sky

speed.doc: how fast the sky wheels about the pole and the stars twinkle

haze.doc: atmosphere — horizon airglow strength and how softly the Milky Way and dust lanes read

glow.doc: the dome-slit thread of light and the low dome of light pollution over the horizon

hue.doc: primary sky hue shift off the default cold blue

x.doc: horizontal position of the celestial pole the sky wheels around, and the light-pollution side

y.doc: the ridge line — how much frame is sky versus dark desert foreground

style.doc: aesthetic: starfield = deep cold night, blue-white stars; milkyway = rich galactic band with a warm core and nebulosity; moonlit = brighter silver sky, fewer stars, domes catch light; chart = abstracted cyan star chart with a polar grid and magnitude rings; ink = abstracted warm-grey ink nocturne, stars as ink points

seed.doc: regenerates the star positions, Milky Way blobs and ridge profile

alpha.doc: layer opacity — sinks the whole sky back behind the performers
